recall.minute: Deployment evolved from apps on bare servers, to VMs with guest operating systems on hypervisors, to containers sharing the host kernel, to Kubernetes orchestrating containers across nodes. ML deployment integrates a model into production behind REST or gRPC, and its components are packaging and containerisation, serving, scalability and orchestration (autoscaling, load balancing, self-healing, rolling updates), and MLOps. Containers package code, runtime, libraries and settings so environments match from dev to prod. Docker builds a Dockerfile (FROM, RUN, COPY, WORKDIR, ENV, EXPOSE, CMD, ENTRYPOINT) into a layered image, runs containers from it and shares images through registries; the client talks to the daemon over a REST API. An ML image holds the model file, API code, dependencies, config and pre/post-processing, and the iris example returns setosa from /predict. Kubernetes, from Google and the CNCF's first graduated project in 2018, has a control plane (API server, etcd, controller manager, scheduler) and workers (kubelet, kube-proxy, runtime); Deployments manage ReplicaSets that manage pods, declared in YAML and applied with kubectl. CI/CD with GitOps uses Jenkins or GitHub Actions to build, a registry to store images, and a deployment repo synced by Argo CD.
